To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

biodegradable poly(L-arginine)/dextran sulfate multilayer capsules can be used for in vivo transport of active compounds, including low-molecular-weight drugs to lung tumors and tumor-promoting macrophages in lung cancer.

we have developed a facile assembly and drug loading technique for biodegradable multilayer polymeric capsules that can be used for targeted therapy of lung cancer via direct erosion of tumor and suppression of the function of tumor-promoting macrophages in tumor microenvironment.

we developed a novel method of drug delivery via biodegradable poly-L-arginine/dextran sulfate multilayer capsules, and we proved that the capsules have a potential to deliver active molecules to both tumor cells and macrophage cells in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new generation of drug carriers with a high potential for clinical applications in cancer therapy.
a facile assembly of biodegradable PMC and their use as a carrier for active molecules in cancer therapy.
a novel approach for delivery of active molecules to the lung tumor microenvironment, which may be further used in injectable drug formulation to treat cancer and other diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we developed a new type of drug delivery system that can be further optimized to be used for treatment of cancer and other diseases.
the developed PMC can serve as a platform for further development of novel drug delivery systems to target lung cancer cells and tumor-promoting macrophages in vivo.
we have developed a facile method for assembly and loading of biodegradable PMC for the treatment of lung cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed PMC are a promising drug carrier for lung cancer treatment, which can be further used as a basis for the development of a novel drug delivery system.
the developed capsules have a great potential for in vivo delivery of drugs for cancer therapy and for targeting of tumor-promoting macrophages in lung cancer.
we have developed a facile method for the preparation of PMC with a potential for in vivo cancer treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PMC can be used for delivery of active molecules of low molecular weight to macrophages and cancer cells, and thus, for the therapy of lung cancer.
the developed PMC may be used as a versatile carrier-system for the treatment of lung cancer, which is one of the deadliest types of cancer, with an estimated mortality of 1.7 million people in 2019.
the developed capsules are capable of delivering drugs to both cancer cells, as well as tumor-associated macrophage, thus, opening new perspectives for cancer therapy.
